title: Terrorist financing diversion
definition: The provision or collection of funds for, or on behalf of, a person or body designated under the sanctions regimes, however small the amounts and whatever the ostensible purpose. The defining feature is the destination, not the mechanism: small, ordinary transactions become material because of whom they reach.
evidence_to_cite: the payment records and the routing through any intermediaries
the screening result that identified the designated party, with its date and source
the stated purpose of the payment and any supporting documentation
benign_explanations: A name match that is a different person with the same name, and was cleared on further evidence.
A payment to a person who shares a surname with a designated party.
A charitable donation to an organisation later designated, made before the designation.
A correspondent bank routing that included a designated party in its chain without that party's knowledge.

sources.citation: Office of Foreign Assets Control, sanctions compliance and reporting guidance, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: Designation status is checked against the date of the transaction, not against today's list. A party designated after the payment does not make the payment reportable, and a party delisted today was still designated then.
